blocks.text: When warned about danger, Tara Singh refuses every language of escape, declaring main tau ab murd pavaun lahaura as though Lahore itself has already become the place where his death will bear witness.

He strengthens that refusal by saying ham áp chahain turkan sir lâî, presenting initiative and courage rather than panic, and then insists that no hiding place can protect a man from the hour appointed for him.

The closing meditation turns proverbial and absolute: jahin jahin jaîai tahîn tahin kala means death meets a person everywhere, so jau kahûn kal tç bhâj kai bachiyat exposes flight as illusion rather than wisdom.
